fault_line: Is Washington rationing Ukraine's shield to fight the Middle East war -- or is Kyiv using the shortage to force a winter package?

sections.what_happened: Zelensky said Ukraine received an average of 12 Patriot interceptor missiles per month from the US throughout 2026, blaming the Middle East war: 'you can count on receiving 150 missiles a year from America, while you need to intercept 150 ballistic missiles every month.' He said Hegseth signed a US package of 12, but 23 missiles sourced from other countries still await Hegseth's signature (transfers need US authorisation); Ukraine used 35 interceptors this month. NASAMS missiles face the same hold. He said he asked Trump in New York (Sep 22) for a winter package and offered not to strike refineries if it were approved. Same briefing cluster (Interfax-Ukraine, Oct 28): the US asked to postpone the planned Brussels meeting (Ukraine/US/EU/NATO secretary general) because US representatives must be in Washington over the Middle East situation. Separately, EU/G7 financing (FT via Ukrainska Pravda, Oct 28): the Commission says NATO states are EUR 13bn short of a EUR 70bn 2026 defence pledge for Ukraine and G7 partners have pledged only EUR 4bn for next year vs the need -- context, not a separate item.
sections.what_verified: Two distinct declared-tier families: Kyiv Independent (T2) and Ukrainska Pravda (T3), both reporting the Oct 27 briefing; NV and Mezha/Interfax-Ukraine carry the same briefing (not counted as additional families). No US confirmation retrieved.
sections.what_disputed: Zelensky is an interested party seeking leverage for a winter package; the US has not confirmed the 12/month figure. Partial offsets exist: European stockpile transfers (pending US sign-off) and the PURL mechanism, under which allies fund US purchases -- so '12 from America' is not Ukraine's total interceptor intake. The Oct 26 Kyiv Independent piece already reported the near-month Hegseth hold, so the hold itself is not new -- only the 12/150/35 numbers are.
sections.why_matters: 12 vs 150: the number that explains why Ukraine's skies are thinning -- and why the refinery-strike pause is priced in missiles, not diplomacy.
sections.context: Background: NEW NUMBERS from Zelensky's Oct 27 briefing, published Oct 28 -- Ukraine gets 12 US Patriot interceptors a month in 2026 vs ~150 ballistic missiles a month to shoot down; 23 more missiles await Hegseth's signature; Ukraine used 35 this month

totw_analysis: Our read: 12 vs 150: the number that explains why Ukraine's skies are thinning -- and why the refinery-strike pause is priced in missiles, not diplomacy. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is Washington rationing Ukraine's shield to fight the Middle East war -- or is Kyiv using the shortage to force a winter package?
